facts.text: Spot gold traded around $4,120/oz on Oct 8, close to a two-month low reached Oct 7.
On Oct 9 gold quotes ranged roughly $4,171–$4,191/oz (Kitco 4,191.50, up $59 on the day; Investing.com 4,183.08; Vantage 4,171.12). Feeds differ by timestamp.
Vantage linked the Oct 9 gold rise to easing oil after President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the 3 November midterm elections.

September FOMC minutes (released Oct 7) showed all 19 policymakers backed September's rate hike, with most seeing another increase as appropriate before year-end; it was the first hike in three years.
The US 10-year Treasury yield hit about 5.35% on Oct 5 (highest since 2002 per sources) and eased to roughly 5.24–5.27% by Oct 8. Levels approximate and vary by site.
The US Dollar Index hit an 18-month high of 102.54 on Oct 5 and closed Oct 8 near 102.1–102.3 (sources differ).
EUR/USD was near 1.121 and USD/JPY near 157.8–158 on Oct 8 (sources differ).
US September CPI is scheduled for Wed Oct 14 at 08:30 ET (15:30 Istanbul time, US daylight time). No survey consensus was found; do not cite one.
Per one calendar: US Retail Sales and PPI (September) are due Thu Oct 15 at 08:30 ET; US bond market is closed Mon Oct 12 for Columbus Day; the next FOMC decision is Wed Oct 28.
